abstractEnglish: We prove the Campana–Peternell inequality $`\kappa(X)\geq\kappa(D)`$ for a smooth connected projective complex variety X and an effective Cartier divisor D whenever $`m_0K_X-D`$ is pseudo-effective for some positive integer m0. For an algebraic fiber space $`f\colon X\to Y`$ between smooth connected projective complex varieties, the hypothesis that $`m_0K_X-f^*H`$ is pseudo-effective with H ample Cartier gives $`\kappa(X)=\kappa(F)+\dim Y`$ for a very general smooth fiber F, as well as nonzero sections of $`mK_X-f^*H`$ for all sufficiently large divisible m.
